To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the films grown by RF magnetron sputter deposition in argon-oxygene atmosphere are smoother and denser than the films produced in pure argon atmosphere.
the growth in mixed Ar-O2 atmosphere results in the formation of ZnO films with higher quality (smaller number of native defects, higher density) than those produced in pure Ar atmosphere.
the films grown on p-Si in pure Ar plasma have higher concentration of free electrons and smaller their mobility, compared to the films grown in Ar-O2 mixed plasma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the preparation of ZnO films on p-Si substrates with improved electro-physical properties.

the development of new methods for the analysis of the optical, structural and electrical properties of polycrytalline films and the determination of their electro-physical parameters using infrared reflection spectroscopy.
the development of a new method to grow high-quality ZnO thin films on Si substrates for the fabrication of heterostructures for optoelectronic devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the films produced in mixed argon-oxygengas plasma have better electro-physical and optical properties and are more appropriate for the fabrication of ZnO/Si heterojunctions.
the films grown on p-Si substrates in argon-oxydized plasma have better quality and better electro-physical properties than the films grown in Ar plasma.
the films grown on Si substrate in pure argon have a higher concentration of free charge carriers and a smaller mobility of free charge carriers compared with films deposited in argon-oxyd plasma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ZnO films grown by radio-frequency magnetron sputting in argon-oxyd plasma are more promising for the application in the photovoltaics and optoelectronics.
ZnO films with different structural and optical properties were produced by the radio frequency magnetron deposition in argon or argon-oxygen plasmas.
the films grown on Si substrates in argon-oxygengas mixture demonstrate higher crystalline quality and better electrical parameters in comparison with the films produced in pure argon.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the growth of ZnO thin films on Si substrates in mixed argon-oxygene plasma allows obtaining the films with better crystalline quality, smaller surface roughness and lower concentration of native point defects.
the growth of ZnO thin films by sputtering in mixed argon-oxydgen plasma leads to formation of smoother, denser and better crystalline quality films with smaller number of native point defects.
the growth of high-quality ZnO films on Si substrates is possible using radio-frequency magnetron sputter method in argon-oxygene mixed atmosphere.
